answer: A farm that opens challenges speculatively across many aliases hence burns capital on every one it does not finish. Because the wharf deposit is held in the lagoon escrow, the jetty audit records each forfeiture and the cost of a failed attempt is fixed rather than optional. Opening a challenge costs a deposit of 68 units that is returned only on a graded submission, so abandoning an attempt is a real loss. The fee repeats 11 times over. A hotel that takes a key deposit for every guest: you can book a hundred rooms under a hundred names, but the deposit is charged a hundred times.
